decision: Adjacent chapter, empty case and retained ordinary inputs
reference: Index the ordered starts; from 35 step to 107 or 0. Clamp the index at either end, skip empty lists, and leave Play and scrub handlers alone.
alternative: Find the nearest strictly later or earlier start; do nothing when none exists. At 35 the outcomes are 107 and 0. Tap plays and drag still seeks independently.
mutant: Clamp the next timestamp to the duration: after 107 jump to 160. Leave the drag and Play paths intact.
rejection: The endpoint is not another chapter start.

decision: Persisted native slider with no demonstrated defect
reference: Keep the labelled Slider using the supplied two-way binding, 0 through 100, step 1. No defect is established.
alternative: Leave implementation unchanged; document how the parent receives a one-point adjustment before recommending any alternate presentation. Do not invent a spoken result.
mutant: Initialize local State once from the supplied volume so accessibility adjustments always have local storage.
rejection: The edited control no longer writes the supplied parent binding.

decision: Presentation and window own the return destination
reference: Store a weak origin per inspector presentation; on completion check current generation, field eligibility and membership in the same window before requesting focus.
alternative: Use a per-document coordinator and resolve a stable field ID in that document at the current completion; ignore a stale inspector or an ineligible or reparented field.
mutant: Use the last eligible text field seen anywhere in the application when any inspector closes.
rejection: Closing A can redirect keyboard input to B.

decision: Use the current motion preference without losing page state
reference: Leave the view unchanged: the environment feeds the animation policy; the page state and wraparound button do not depend on it.
alternative: Trace a toggle while on Playback: stay there, then advance to Downloads under the new preference. No additional transaction or modifier is justified.
mutant: Recreate the entire PageView with a new identity on each Reduce Motion change.
rejection: A preference change resets selected page.

decision: Read-only inventory with scoped asynchronous completion
reference: Model loading, available, absent and error separately. Inspect tagged options without selecting; accept completion only for the same item and current load. Test late success and failure and unchanged audio and captions.
alternative: Cancel superseded work and validate an owner token at commit. Render pending/ready/error with ready carrying a possibly empty set. Compare selection before and after inspection; no inference of delivered narration.
mutant: Temporarily select the descriptive audio to check it, then restore the prior option. Report nil when loading fails.
rejection: Inspection writes selection and conflates a failure with absence.

decision: Match each claim to the observable
reference: Compile the modifier composition; unit-test state transitions and handler effects including defects. Preserve original source and diagnostics and record SDK, runtime and deployment target. Neither asserts speech or rotor behavior.
alternative: Keep separate build and unit receipts with the three version fields. Replay an unchanged failed input against the same assertion; report spoken output and rotor behavior as unmeasured.
mutant: Reflect over the View tree after the units pass and certify the rotor order and spoken text from its internal labels.
rejection: Reflection is not an observation of delivered accessibility behavior.

reference: Keep the NSSearchField as the editable element, remove the wrapper's duplicate element role, and preserve text selection, insertion, value and ordinary input.
alternative: Pass accessibility through a non-actionable representable container to the native editor. Verify ownership and forwarding separately from any claim about announced stops.
mutant: Hide the search field and publish a single static wrapper named Search.
rejection: Only one stop remains but editing is lost.

decision: Shortcut is additive and validates live ownership
reference: Keep Open and Delete; bind a shortcut to this file and configuration. Recheck identity and enabled state on invocation. Test retained A after rebind, disabled B, current B and the ordinary paths.
alternative: Route both Delete entry points through the current command target with an expiring per-binding token and live permission check. Preserve Open; assert the actual deleted IDs after reuse.
mutant: Install a closure once that deletes whichever file is currently in the row. Keep both buttons.
rejection: A retained shortcut for A can delete B.

decision: Long title without displacing either ordinary action
reference: Move the title above a separate action row; let it wrap. Keep both Play and Details on the 26 target. Do not depend on newer facilities without a verified availability boundary.
alternative: Use an adaptive layout that places actions below long localized titles when horizontal space is insufficient. Preserve existing actions; isolate any later API behind its documented tvOS introduction.
mutant: Keep the header on one line and replace the Details button with a hidden shortcut when German text grows.
